name: italian tomato sauce
instructions:
THE ITALIAN TOMATO SAUCE HOUSE — the protein-free tomato pasta sauces. Merged 2026-11-13 from the red pasta sauces; [[bolognese]] and [[spaghetti-and-meatballs]] split back OUT into their own files 2026-11-18:
- VARIANT A — MARCELLA GNOCCHI SAUCE: the 3-ingredient butter-onion-tomato sauce (pass).
- VARIANT A — VODKA SAUCE: the cream branch, gigi hadid style (revived 2026-11-13 from the september retirement; pre-retirement verdict was 'excellent').
- VARIANT C — SUPERMARKET PORCINI SAUCE: marcella-inspired (her 'tomato sauce with porcini mushrooms'), heavily modified (added 2026-11-17, pass).

(Weeknight vegetarian ragu and pasta piperade RETIRED 2026-11-18, both in retired/. Re-lettered twice that day — once after the retirements, once after the split. See notes.)

THE TOMATO FORMS SPLIT HARD BY BUILD — see the build-dependent rulings note before substituting anything.

=== VARIANT A — MARCELLA GNOCCHI SAUCE (THE 3-INGREDIENT SAUCE — PASS) ===

Marcella Hazan's famous three-ingredient tomato sauce, kept in the cookbook as THE GNOCCHI SAUCE — she recommends the basic tomato/onion/butter sauce be used on GNOCCHI in particular, and it's very simple, requiring no blender. From Essentials of Classic Italian Cooking.

(The rest of the tomato pasta sauce family — sicilian pesto rosso, marcella eggplant sauce, and (as of 2026-11-18, again) pasta piperade — is RETIRED to retired/; vodka sauce was revived 2026-11-13 as variant B.)

=== INGREDIENTS ===

- 28-oz can whole peeled tomatoes (San Marzano ideal — canned whole, not diced, not paste)
- 1 medium yellow onion, peeled and halved (NOT chopped — kept in halves)
- 5 tablespoons unsalted butter
- salt to taste
- gnocchi (Marcella's recommended pairing — the reason this recipe survives; short pasta shapes also fine)

=== PROCEDURE ===

1. Combine tomatoes, butter, onion halves, and a pinch of salt in a saucepan.
2. Simmer uncovered on low for ~45 minutes, stirring occasionally and crushing the tomatoes with the back of a spoon as they soften.
3. Fish out and discard the onion halves before serving (they've done their aromatic job).
4. Toss with cooked gnocchi (or short pasta).

=== VARIANT B — VODKA SAUCE (THE CREAM BRANCH — REVIVED) ===

A DIFFERENT BRANCH of the tomato-sauce family — this one adds heavy cream. Structurally it belongs somewhere between the pure-tomato family and a cream sauce. It's grouped here because the sauce is fundamentally a tomato dish that happens to add cream, not a cream dish that happens to add tomato. Gigi Hadid style.

INGREDIENTS:
- 1 medium yellow onion, finely chopped
- 3-4 cloves garlic, minced
- 2-3 tablespoons butter
- 2-3 tablespoons olive oil
- 4-6 tablespoons tomato paste (concentrated)
- 1/4 cup vodka
- 1/2 to 3/4 cup heavy whipping cream
- red chili flakes (canonical here — the gigi hadid version leans on them)
- grated parmesan cheese
- fresh basil (torn, off heat)
- salt to taste
- pasta (short shapes — penne or fusilli (2026-11-18); the revival text said penne/rigatoni)

PROCEDURE:
1. Sauté onion and garlic in butter + olive oil until softened.
2. Add tomato paste and cook it hard in the fat until it darkens a shade and smells sweet-caramelized (~3-5 min). This is the load-bearing flavor step.
3. Pour in vodka; let it reduce briefly (~2 min).
4. Stir in heavy cream and red chili flakes. Simmer to combine.
5. Off heat, fold in grated parmesan and torn fresh basil. Salt to taste.
6. Toss with cooked short pasta.

=== VARIANT C — SUPERMARKET PORCINI SAUCE (MARCELLA-INSPIRED — PASS; RENAMED 2026-11-18, TWICE, FROM 'TOMATO SAUCE WITH PORCINI MUSHROOMS') ===

FOR 4 SERVINGS.

INGREDIENTS:
- 2 tablespoons shallot OR onion chopped fine
- 2 1/2 tablespoons butter
- 1 tablespoon vegetable oil
- 2 tablespoons pancetta, prosciutto, OR unsmoked ham, cut into 1/4-inch-wide strips
- 1 1/2 cups fresh, ripe tomatoes, peeled and chopped, OR canned imported Italian plum tomatoes, cut up, with their juice
- A small packet OR 1 ounce dried porcini mushrooms, reconstituted (her page-28 method)
- The filtered water from the mushroom soak (also page 28)
- Salt
- Black pepper, ground fresh from the mill
- 1 pound pasta
- Freshly grated parmigiano-reggiano cheese for the table

RECOMMENDED PASTA: conchiglie, penne, ridged ziti, or a substantial fresh pasta such as tonnarelli or pappardelle. Serve with grated Parmesan.

PROCEDURE:
1. Put the shallot or onion into a saucepan together with all the butter and oil, and turn on the heat to medium. Cook and stir the shallot or onion until it becomes colored a pale gold. Add the strips of pancetta or ham, and cook for 1 or 2 minutes, stirring from time to time.
2. Add the cut-up tomatoes with their juice, the reconstituted mushrooms, the strained liquid from the mushroom soak, salt, and several grindings of pepper. Adjust heat so that the sauce bubbles at a gentle, but steady simmer. Cook in the uncovered pan for about 40 minutes, until the fat and the tomato separate, stirring occasionally.
3. After tossing the pasta with the sauce, serve with freshly grated Parmesan on the side.

MY NOTES:
- PORCINI MUSHROOM POWDER IS FINE in place of the reconstituted dried porcini.
- I like putting it in the BLENDER and UNDERBLENDING it — just chunk it.
- SHE ADDS THE MEAT (the pancetta/prosciutto/ham), which gives it UMAMI — I generally DON'T, so it needs the extra TOMATO PASTE or NOOCH (I add a little of both).
- I like to add FINELY MINCED/CRUSHED BASIL and 1/2 TABLESPOON OF SUGAR to make it more like a SUPERMARKET PASTA SAUCE — in a good way. It is the closest approximation of a supermarket pasta sauce, tbh.
- BEST EATEN WITH SPAGHETTI.
- TOMATO FORM: CANNED CHUNKY TOMATO is best, with TOMATO PASTE TO TITRATE UMAMI — there's a blender phase, and you can keep some of the tomato chunks (mid-blended) for a nice consistency.
- HER FAT PAIR — BUTTER + VEGETABLE OIL — is SUBTLE AND BRILLIANT: the butter is for FLAVOR, the vegetable oil is for TEXTURE. Olive oil wouldn't work as well.
notes:
=== THE TOMATO SAUCE HOUSE — MERGE AND SPLIT HISTORY ===

The red pasta sauces merged into one house 2026-11-13; the protein-forward side split back out 2026-11-18 ([[bolognese]], [[spaghetti-and-meatballs]]). What remains is the protein-free side: A the gnocchi sauce, B the vodka sauce (cream branch), C the supermarket porcini sauce (marcella-inspired).

=== RETIRED 2026-11-18 — WEEKNIGHT VEGETARIAN RAGU AND PASTA PIPERADE ===

Both removed to retired/ (pre-merge originals recovered from git). The weeknight vegetarian ragu is just an intuitive leftover sauce — not really a recipe. Pasta piperade: I think I can cook better things now and it's not really the best pasta sauce. (Piperade's SECOND retirement — retired September 2026, unretired the same month because it kept getting made, re-retired now.) RE-LETTERED same day: the house is now A–E (old C→B gnocchi sauce, old D→C spaghetti and meatballs, old F→D vodka sauce, old G→E Marcella's porcini sauce; the bolognese's brief inner A1/A2 split was collapsed into footnotes the same day). The retired variants' old letters (weeknight ragu was B, piperade was E) survive only in git history and the retired/ files.

=== SPLIT BACK OUT 2026-11-18 — BOLOGNESE AND SPAGHETTI AND MEATBALLS ===

Turning the house back into multiple recipes: [[bolognese]] (was variant A) and [[spaghetti-and-meatballs]] (was variant C) have their own files again, near-verbatim. The remaining variants re-lettered a second time: gnocchi B→A, vodka D→B, porcini E→C.

=== TOMATO RULING — ALL ITALIAN TOMATO SAUCES (2026-11-18) ===

FRESH TOMATOES ARE TOO RAW AND SOUR — they don't give enough umami on their own. CANNED CHUNKY TOMATOES WITH TOMATO PASTE, or CANNED TOMATO SAUCE, are ideal. FIRE-ROASTED canned tomatoes aren't right either — they have a better flavor profile for MEXICAN and INDIAN food. (Fresh and fire-roasted tomatoes moved to clashing accordingly. Marcella's variant C transcription keeps her fresh-or-canned wording verbatim, but the canned path is the ruling.)

=== BUILD-DEPENDENT RULINGS (READ BEFORE SUBSTITUTING) ===

- TOMATO FORMS (updated 2026-11-18): A works best with CANNED TOMATO SAUCE — no blender phase (Marcella's canonical canned-whole kept in the transcription). C takes CANNED CHUNKY TOMATO + TOMATO PASTE to titrate umami (blender phase; keep some chunks mid-blended). TOMATO PASTE is structural in B, a little in C. DICED TOMATOES clashing (A's ruling). FRESH TOMATOES: CLASHING (the all-sauces ruling above). FIRE-ROASTED: also clashing per the same ruling.
- PASTA PAIRINGS (2026-11-18): A = GNOCCHI (obviously), B = PENNE or FUSILLI, C = SPAGHETTI.
- ONIONS: yellow onions are core to A/B; C takes shallot OR onion.
- GARLIC + OLIVE OIL: the vodka sauce's (B). A (Marcella's 3-ingredient) is butter-only — no garlic, and basil is clashing there too; C has no garlic either (shallot + butter + oil).
- CREAM: structural in B (the vodka-sauce branch) — primary now that the clashing builds left the house.

=== VARIANT A — MARCELLA GNOCCHI SAUCE (THE 3-INGREDIENT SAUCE — PASS) — NOTES ===

Marcella Hazan's 3-ingredient tomato sauce (Essentials of Classic Italian Cooking). Split out from the former italian-tomato-sauces.json (Variant A) into its own file, and RENAMED 'MARCELLA GNOCCHI SAUCE' (September 2026): she recommends this basic tomato/onion/butter sauce for GNOCCHI in particular, and it's very simple — no blender required. That's the niche that kept it on the menu when the rest of the tomato-sauce family retired.

=== THE REST OF THE FAMILY IS RETIRED ===

Sicilian pesto rosso, vodka sauce, and marcella eggplant sauce were moved to retired/ (pasta piperade went too but was later unretired — it kept getting made) (September 2026). (Update 2026-11-18: piperade is RE-RETIRED — I can cook better things now; vodka sauce came back as variant B on 2026-11-13.): they just never make it onto the menu — the amount of effort required for very little nutrition, and awkward leftovers. This sauce survives on the opposite math: minimal effort, no blender, and a specific job (gnocchi).

=== WHY IT WORKS WITH ONLY THREE INGREDIENTS ===

Hazan's insight is that a whole peeled canned tomato + butter + onion, given enough time (~45 min uncovered), builds a sauce that reads more complex than the ingredient list suggests. Butter adds richness and rounds acidity in a way olive oil can't at this simplicity. The onion halves perfume the sauce without becoming a chunky component — that's why they go in whole and come out before serving. No garlic, no basil, no oregano, no chili — the restraint is the recipe.

=== DON'T CHOP THE ONION ===

The onion halves are meant to be discarded. Chopping the onion turns it into part of the sauce texture and changes the dish.

=== UNSALTED BUTTER, GENEROUS ===

Hazan calls for 5 tablespoons per 28-oz can. Don't cut it — the butter is doing structural work, not just flavor. Unsalted so you control the seasoning.

=== SAN MARZANO IF POSSIBLE ===

Whole peeled San Marzano tomatoes are what the recipe was tuned to. Other whole peeled canned tomatoes work; diced canned tomatoes read watery here.

=== MY NOTE — CANNED TOMATO SAUCE OVER CHUNKY (2026-11-18) ===

I think this works best with CANNED TOMATO SAUCE rather than chunky tomato, because there can be NO BLENDER PHASE in this sauce. (Marcella's canonical canned-whole stays in the transcription; the supermarket porcini sauce is the opposite call — it has a blender phase, so chunky wins there.)

=== FORMER SIBLINGS (ALL IN retired/) ===

- sicilian-pesto-rosso: raw blended sun-dried-tomato + almond pesto.
- vodka-sauce: tomato paste + cream cross-family outlier (revived 2026-11-13 as variant B).
- pasta-piperade: blended vegetable-tomato base — unretired September 2026 (it kept getting made), RE-RETIRED 2026-11-18.
- marcella-eggplant-sauce: fried eggplant folded into a garlic-tomato base. Also Marcella.

=== DIFFERENTIATION FROM THE RAGU FAMILY ===

This recipe and its siblings tagged 'tomato pasta sauce' are deliberately narrow — protein-free tomato sauces, whole-or-blended (never knife-diced into discrete chunks). For protein-forward, long-simmered, cutting-board-cut counterparts, see the ragu family: [[bolognese]] and [[spaghetti-and-meatballs]].

=== VARIANT B — VODKA SAUCE — NOTES ===

Retired september 2026 in the tomato-sauces purge, revived 2026-11-13 as a variant here. Pre-retirement verdict was 'excellent'. Gigi Hadid-style version — heavy on the chili flakes.

SITS ON A DIFFERENT BRANCH: the other builds stay on the tomato axis; this one adds heavy cream and moves toward a cross-family space between italian tomato and cream sauces. It still belongs in this house because the tomato paste + tomato register does the flavor work — a tomato sauce that happens to add cream, not a cream sauce that happens to add tomato.

TOMATO PASTE IS THE TOMATO SOURCE — LOAD-BEARING: paste cooked hard in the fat until it darkens is the main tomato base — opposite of the gnocchi sauce (variant A, canned whole). COOK IT HARD: the darken-and-caramelize step (~3-5 min) is where the flavor comes from; under-cook it and the sauce tastes tinny and raw.

RED CHILI FLAKES CANONICAL: the gigi hadid version leans on them. Not optional here. Adjust to taste but include them.

SHORT PASTA — PENNE OR FUSILLI (updated 2026-11-18; the revival text said penne/rigatoni): the thick creamy sauce needs short shapes that grip. Long strands slide out from under it.

FRESH BASIL AT THE END: torn, folded in off heat — basil wilts fast and turns brown if you cook it. (Basil stays clashing in variant A.)

=== VARIANT C — SUPERMARKET PORCINI SAUCE (MARCELLA-INSPIRED — PASS) — NOTES ===

RENAMED 2026-11-18 from 'tomato sauce with porcini mushrooms' (her book title, kept in the credit) — first to 'marcella's porcini basil sauce', then settled as SUPERMARKET PORCINI SAUCE the same day: the build is MARCELLA-INSPIRED (butter + vegetable oil, onion without garlic, porcini mushrooms) but HEAVILY MODIFIED — tomato paste, sugar, and basil added, the meat skipped. Her verbatim transcription stays below as the source. Added 2026-11-17, transcribed verbatim from Essentials of Classic Italian Cooking (pasta chapter, p. 163). Her mushroom component is WHOLE RECONSTITUTED DRIED PORCINI plus the strained soak liquid — no fresh mushrooms. PORCINI MUSHROOM POWDER IS FINE in place of the reconstituted porcini (my ruling).

Her signals: shallot or onion to PALE GOLD in the butter + oil before the pancetta/ham goes in; 40 minutes uncovered at a gentle, steady simmer, done when THE FAT AND THE TOMATO SEPARATE (the same fat-separation doneness signal as [[bolognese]]'s ragu).

MY BUILD (PASS): I like putting it in the BLENDER and UNDERBLENDING it — just chunk it, not smooth. And I add a little TOMATO PASTE and NOOCH.

THE MEAT IS THE UMAMI — AND I SKIP IT: she adds the meat, which gives it umami. I generally DON'T, so it NEEDS the extra tomato paste or nooch (pancetta moved to secondary on this basis — her canonical, my skip).

THE SUPERMARKET SAUCE MOVE: I like to add FINELY MINCED/CRUSHED BASIL and 1/2 TABLESPOON OF SUGAR to make it more like a SUPERMARKET PASTA SAUCE — in a good way. It is the closest approximation of a supermarket pasta sauce tbh.

PAIRING: BEST EATEN WITH SPAGHETTI. (Her recommended list — conchiglie, penne, ridged ziti, tonnarelli, pappardelle — stays in the transcription.)

TOMATO FORM (2026-11-18): CANNED CHUNKY TOMATO is best here, with TOMATO PASTE TO TITRATE UMAMI — because there IS a blender phase, and you can keep some of the tomato chunks (mid-blended) to make a nice consistency. (Contrast the gnocchi sauce, which has NO blender phase and wants canned tomato sauce.)

BUTTER + VEGETABLE OIL — SUBTLE AND BRILLIANT: Marcella uses both, and it's subtle and brilliant — the BUTTER is for FLAVOR, the VEGETABLE OIL is for TEXTURE, and OLIVE OIL WOULDN'T WORK AS WELL.
original_chef: Variant A: Marcella Hazan — the 3-ingredient tomato sauce. Variant B: Gigi Hadid style (viral home-cook version of a standard italian-american vodka sauce). Variant C: Marcella Hazan — Tomato Sauce with Porcini Mushrooms (Essentials of Classic Italian Cooking).
